22.14: What adulterous women say is as dangerous as a deep hole that men could fall into; those with whom Yahweh is angry will suffer from it. \
22.15: Children naturally think foolishly, but physically disciplining them will teach them to stop being foolish.
22.16: People who oppress poor people in order to make more money for themselves or who give things to rich people in order to become rich will only become poor. \
22.17: Listen carefully to what wise people have said; consider carefully what I am teaching you!
22.18: Do this because if you remember these sayings and if you are always ready to repeat them to others, then you will be glad.
22.19: I am teaching these sayings to you — yes, you — right now so that you will trust Yahweh. \
22.20: I am indeed writing these 30 sayings to advise and teach you.
22.21: I am writing them in order to teach you what is true in trustworthy sayings, and in order to answer those who sent you with trustworthy sayings. \
22.22: Do not steal from poor people just because they are poor; and do not oppress suffering people in court.
22.23: Do not do these things because Yahweh will defend those poor people when you dispute with them, and he will kill the people who stole from them. \
22.24: Do not become friends with angry people. Indeed, do not associate with people who easily become angry.
22.25: If you do so, then you will act like them, and you will endanger yourself like an animal caught in a trap. \
22.26: Stay away from those people who agree to pay loans for others. Indeed, stay away from those people who guarantee to pay the loans of others.
22.27: Because if you cannot pay back the loan, then the person to whom you owe money will surely take away even your own bed in order to pay back the loan. \
22.28: Do not cheat people by moving the stones that their ancestors placed long ago to mark the boundaries of their land.
22.29: Consider this: People who work skillfully will serve kings rather than serving unknown people. \

23.1: When you sit down to eat a meal with someone who rules over others, pay attention to the food that is in front of you.
23.2: Restrain yourself from eating too much if you like eating a lot of food.
23.3: Do not crave the expensive food that the ruler has because that ruler is using that food to deceive you. \
23.4: Do not work so much that you exhaust yourself in order to become rich. Be understanding enough to stop doing so.
23.5: As soon as you look at that wealth, it will surely be gone! This is because wealth certainly disappears quickly as if it had wings and flew off into the sky like a fast bird. \
23.6: Do not eat food that stingy people give you. Do not crave the expensive food that they have,
23.7: because stingy people are always thinking about how much the food costs them. They will tell you to eat and drink, but they do not mean what they say.
23.8: When you realize this, you will want to vomit what little food you ate. You will have wasted the kind things you said to them. \
23.9: Do not try to talk to foolish people because they will only despise the insightful things that you say.
23.10: Do not cheat people by moving the old stones that mark the boundaries of their land. Do not claim the land that belongs to defenseless orphans,
23.11: because Yahweh is the one who redeems them and he is powerful. He is the one who will defend them when they dispute with you. \
23.12: Consider carefully what people say when they correct you. Indeed, listen carefully to what people teach you. \
23.13: Do not refuse to discipline your children. If you physically punish them, they will not die.
23.14: In fact, if you physically punish your children, you will prevent them from dying. \
23.15: My child, if you are wise, then surely I myself will be very happy,
23.16: and I will be deeply joyful when you say what is right. \
23.17: Do not envy sinful people; instead always revere Yahweh.
23.18: If you do so, then you will surely have a good future, and what you hope will happen will indeed occur! \
23.19: My child, listen to me so that you can become wise. Make yourself think about behaving rightly.
23.20: Stay away from drunkards and gluttons,
23.21: because drunkards and gluttons will become poor. They sleep so much that they will only have rags to wear. \
23.22: Pay attention to your father, who enabled you to exist, and continue to honor your mother when she becomes old.
23.23: Learn what is true and remember it. Learn what is wise and instructive and what you should understand. \
23.24: Fathers of righteous people are very joyful. Indeed, those who father wise people are happy because of them.
23.25: So do what will make your parents happy! Do what will make your mother joyful! \
23.26: My son, pay close attention to me! Carefully observe what I do!
23.27: Do this because prostitutes are as dangerous as a deep hole. Indeed, becoming involved with an adulterous woman is as dangerous as falling into a well that you cannot escape from.
23.28: These very women certainly wait for men to seduce like robbers wait for people to rob. They cause many men to become unfaithful. \
23.29: These are the kind of people who are woeful, sorrowful, and quarrelsome, who lament, get hurt for no reason, and have red eyes:
23.30: those people who drink too much wine and are always looking around for wine to drink that someone has prepared. \
23.31: Do not let wine become overly attractive to you, even though it is beautifully red, glistens in the cup, and goes down your throat smoothly.
23.32: Afterward you will feel as terrible as if a poisonous snake has bitten you.
23.33: When you are drunk, you will hallucinate, and you will imagine distorted things. \
23.34: You will feel dizzy and sick as if you were trying to sleep on a ship that the sea was tossing back and forth. Indeed, you will feel as if you were trying to sleep while swaying at the top of a ship’s sails.
23.35: You will say, “People hit me, but it did not hurt. People beat me, but I did not feel it. I wish I could be sober so that I could find even more wine to drink again!” \

24.1: Do not envy evil people; do not want to associate with them,
24.2: because they plan to act violently, and they talk about doing bad things to people. \
24.3: People build households by acting wisely; they make those households stable by acting sensibly.
24.4: By acting knowledgeably, people fill the rooms of those households with all kinds of valuable and delightful riches. \
24.5: Wise people are strong, and knowledgeable people make themselves more powerful,
24.6: because letting people advise you will make you fight your war successfully, and letting many people counsel you will rescue you from losing the war. \
24.7: Foolish people cannot understand what is wise; they have nothing useful to say in court. \
24.8: Some people are always planning to do evil things; people refer to them as schemers.
24.9: Foolish plans are sinful, and people detest those who ridicule others. \
24.10: If you give up during distressful times, then you are weak. \
24.11: Save people whom others are trying to kill; save the ones who will certainly die unless you do something!
24.12: If you falsely claim that you did not know that those people were dying unjustly, then think about this: Yahweh knows exactly what you are thinking and he understands what you are doing! He is the one who keeps you alive and he knows everything about you! He will surely make people receive what they deserve for whatever they have done or not done! \
24.13: My child, eat honey because it tastes good, and honey dripping from the comb tastes sweet.
24.14: Be aware that what is wise is like honey for you. If you become wise, then you will have a good future, and what you hope will happen will indeed occur! \
24.15: Do not be like wicked people and hide in wait in order to attack the places where righteous people dwell. Do not devastate the places where righteous people rest!
24.16: Do not do so because righteous people can recover many times when disastrous things happen to them, but disastrous things will destroy wicked people. \
24.17: Do not be happy when something disastrous happens to your adversaries. Indeed, do not rejoice when that happens!
24.18: If you do, then Yahweh will notice and disapprove, so that he stops being angry with your enemies. \
24.19: Do not worry about people who do what is evil. Do not be envious of wicked people.
24.20: Do not do so because evil people will not have good futures, but wicked people will merely die like an oil lamp that stops burning oil. \
24.21: My child, reverently fear Yahweh and kings. Avoid people who rebel against either Yahweh or the king,
24.22: because disastrous things will happen quickly to those people, and no one knows how terribly both Yahweh and kings can destroy others! \
24.23: Here are more things that wise people have said: It is very evil to favor someone when you judge. \
24.24: If anyone declares that a guilty person is innocent, many people will curse him and whole people groups will hate him.
24.25: However, people who condemn guilty people will prosper, and Yahweh will bless them well. \
24.26: People who answer honestly show that they are true friends.
24.27: Do the work you must do outside and prepare your fields before you build your house. \
24.28: Do not testify against someone if you do not have a good reason to do so, and do not try to deceive people by what you say.
24.29: Do not say, “I will do to him that same bad thing that he did to me; I will pay him back for what he did to me!” \
24.30: I walked by the land of a lazy person and past the vineyard of someone who does not think wisely.
24.31: And I saw that thistles and weeds were everywhere in that field and vineyard. Even the stone wall surrounding them had fallen down. \
24.32: When I saw that, I considered carefully what I was seeing. When I observed that, I learned this:
24.33: If you say to yourself, “Let me sleep just a little more! Let me lay my hands across my chest in order to rest comfortably for a little while longer!”
24.34: Then the result of being so lazy will be that you will become poor and needy just as surely as if a thief has robbed you. \

25.1: Here are more wise sayings said by Solomon that the scribes who served Hezekiah, the king of Judah, copied from a scroll that Solomon had written:
25.2: God shows how glorious he is when he makes something that is difficult for people to understand. But kings show how glorious they are when they explain something that is difficult for people to understand.
25.3: As people cannot fully understand how high the sky is or how deep the earth is, so they cannot fully understand what kings think. \
25.4: People who make things from metal must remove impurities from silver before they can make that silver into something useful.
25.5: In the same way, people must remove wicked advisers from the presence of kings so that they can rule securely by being righteous. \
25.6: Do not promote yourself in front of kings, and do not pretend to be great. \
25.7: Do not do so because it is better if someone invites you to sit in a place that is closer to the king, than for someone to embarrass you in front of a royal official whom you have seen by telling you to sit farther away from the king.
25.8: Do not plead your case too quickly against someone you know. If you do, then you will not know what to do when that person wins the case and embarrasses you! \
25.9: If you do indeed plead your case against someone you know, settle it between yourselves and do not tell others any secret about that person.
25.10: If you do tell a secret, then the people who hear you may shame you for it, and people will speak badly about you from then on. \
25.11: When someone says something that is very appropriate to a situation, it is as delightful as seeing golden apples in a setting of silver.
25.12: When a wise person rebukes someone who is willing to listen, it is as valuable as a gold ring or jewelry made from the best gold. \
25.13: Reliable messengers are as refreshing to those who send them as cold snow would be refreshing during the summer harvest time; they refresh the people whom they serve.
25.14: People who brag about giving something but then do not give it are as disappointing as clouds and wind that do not bring rain. \
25.15: People can persuade leaders by being patient, and by speaking gently people can convince those who oppose them to agree with them. \
25.16: If you discover some wild honey, do not eat too much of it. If you do, then you will become sick from it and vomit.
25.17: In the same way, do not visit too often the houses of your friends. If you do, then they may feel that they have had too much of you and even hate you. \
25.18: People who lie when they testify against other people are deadly, as if they had attacked them with a club, a sword, or a piercing arrow.
25.19: Trusting treacherous people during distressful times is like trying to eat with a rotten tooth or trying to walk with a crippled foot. \
25.20: Singing songs to someone who is sad is as unhelpful as taking a coat off of someone in cold weather or pouring vinegar on soda. \
25.21: Feed your enemies if they are hungry; give them something to drink if they are thirsty.
25.22: Do so because by doing so you will shame them, as if you were pouring burning coals on top of them, and Yahweh will reward you for doing so. \
25.23: When wind blows from the north, that produces rain. Similarly, when people tell the secrets of others, that produces angry people.
25.24: It is better to live alone in a corner of a housetop than to live inside a house with a wife who always argues with you. \
25.25: When people hear something good from a faraway place, it is as refreshing as drinking cold water when one is thirsty.
25.26: When righteous people yield to wicked people, it is as bad as a spring that people have made murky by walking in it or as bad as a polluted fountain. \
25.27: As it is not good to eat too much honey; so it is not honorable to try to make people honor you.
25.28: People who cannot control themselves are as defenseless as a city that an army has broken into and knocked down its walls. \

26.1: Honoring foolish people is just as inappropriate as snow falling in hot summer and rain falling during the time to harvest crops.
26.2: Just as a bird will fly by and not land on you, so a curse will not harm you if you are innocent. \
26.3: As people must whip horses and bridle donkeys in order to guide them, so people must physically punish foolish people in order to guide them.
26.4: Do not reply to foolish people according to their foolish way of thinking. If you do, then you also will be foolish. \
26.5: Reply to foolish people according to their foolish way of thinking. If you do not, then they may think that they are wise.
26.6: Anyone who asks a foolish person to take a message to someone is doing something as foolish as cutting off his own feet or drinking poison. \
26.7: As the legs of people who cannot walk are useless, so are the sayings that foolish people say.
26.8: Honoring foolish people is just as useless as a harmless weapon. \
26.9: A drunken person picks up a thorn and it will hurt someone, in the same way a foolish person says a proverb that can only be harmful.
26.10: People who employ foolish people or random strangers are as dangerous as someone who randomly shoots arrows at people. \
26.11: Foolish people who do the same foolish thing over and over again are like dogs that eat what they have vomited up.
26.12: Consider this: Foolish people are more likely to learn than people who wrongly think that they are already wise. \
26.13: Lazy people claim that there is a lion in the path or in the midst of the streets so that they can stay inside their houses and do nothing.
26.14: As doors swing on their hinges and do not go anywhere, so lazy people turn back and forth in their beds. \
26.15: Lazy people put their hands in a dish of food, but they are so lazy that they will not lift the food to their mouths.
26.16: A typical lazy person wrongly thinks that he is wiser than several people who answer intelligently. \
26.17: People who make themselves angry because of an argument that does not concern them are as foolish as people who grab the ears of a dog that is passing by. \
26.18: People who trick others and then say that they were just joking are as dangerous as a crazy person who shoots deadly flaming arrows at people. \
26.19: People who trick others and then say that they were just joking are as dangerous as a crazy person who shoots deadly flaming arrows at people. \
26.20: Fires stop burning when they have nothing to burn. In the same way, people stop arguing when no one is gossiping.
26.21: As charcoal keeps coals burning and wood keeps fires burning, so people who always argue keep other people arguing. \
26.22: People are eager to listen to what people who gossip say, and what they say deeply affects those who hear it.
26.23: People who fervently say that they are your friend while thinking about doing evil things to you are as deceptive as a cheap clay pot that someone has made to look like silver. \
26.24: People who hate you will use what they say to hide what they feel, but they are really thinking about how to betray you.
26.25: Do not believe those people when they speak kindly to you, because they are thinking many detestable things.
26.26: Although those people deceive others by pretending that they do not hate you, When people gather together, they will discover how wicked those people are. \
26.27: People who dig pits to trap others will fall into those pits instead; and people who try to crush others with stones will become crushed by those stones instead.
26.28: Liars hate the people whom they hurt, and flatterers cause disastrous things to happen. \

27.1: Do not brag about what you will do tomorrow, because you do not know what will happen then.
27.2: Do not praise yourself; let someone else praise you. Indeed, let other people praise you, not yourself. \
27.3: Stones and sand are heavy, but fools are so annoying that they are harder to bear than either of those.
27.4: Angry people are cruel and furious people are destructive, but no one can withstand jealous people! \
27.5: It is better to correct people openly, than to love them without showing them that you love them.
27.6: Friends will be faithful to you by criticizing you when necessary, but enemies will deceive you by acting affectionately toward you. \
27.7: When people have full stomachs, they do not want to eat even honey. But when people are hungry, even bitter things taste sweet to them.
27.8: People who stray from their homes are like birds that stray from their nests. \
27.9: Fragrant oil and perfume make people feel happy, but having a friend who advises you sincerely is even better.
27.10: Do not ignore your friends or your father’s friends. Do not think that you must go to the house of a relative when something disastrous happens to you. Rather, it is better to go to a nearby neighbor than to relatives who live far away. \
27.11: My child, make me happy by becoming wise. Then I will be able to reply to anyone who argues against me.
27.12: Sensible people observe something dangerous happening and avoid it, but naive people ignorantly do not avoid it and suffer for doing so. \
27.13: Take the coats of people who promise to pay a loan for someone whom they do not know. Indeed, hold onto the coats of people who do so for a foreigner.
27.14: If you rise early in the morning and loudly call out a blessing to your neighbor while he is still sleeping, he will consider it to be a curse, not a blessing. \
27.15: A wife who always argues with you is as annoying as constantly dripping water on a rainy day.
27.16: It is as difficult to stop her from arguing as stopping the wind, or catching oil in one hand. \
27.17: We can use one iron tool to sharpen another iron tool; similarly, when one person shares what he is thinking, it can help another person to think more clearly.
27.18: Just as people who take care of fruit trees will also eat the fruit from those trees, so too will masters honor their servants who guard them. \
27.19: When people look in water, the water reflects their faces. In the same way, what people think reveals what kinds of people they are.
27.20: Just as the place where dead people go never becomes full; so people never stop wanting things. \
27.21: People use crucibles and furnaces to test and refine silver and gold. In the same way, people can know what kind of person someone is by how he reacts when people praise him.
27.22: If you were to crush a fool the way that you would crush grain into powder, you would still not be able to find any part of him that is not foolish. \
27.23: Be fully aware of how your sheep are doing. Indeed, consider carefully how your animals fare.
27.24: Do so because riches will not last forever. Even a king’s family will not rule forever!
27.25: Harvest the grass and then you will see new grass. Collect and store the plants that grow on the hillside. \
27.26: If you do these things, then you will have lambs with wool that you can clothe yourself with. You will also have male goats that you can sell for enough money to buy a field.
27.27: You will even have female goats that produce enough milk for yourself, your family, and your servant girls to drink. \

28.1: Wicked people run away even though no one is chasing them, but righteous people are as brave as lions.
28.2: When the people in a country sin, they will continually have new leaders; but when they have a truly knowledgeable ruler, then they will have a stable government that will last. \
28.3: A poor person who oppresses other poor people is as destructive as rain that washes away the crops, leaving nothing to eat.
28.4: People who reject Yahweh’s laws say good things about wicked people; but people who obey those laws oppose such wicked people. \
28.5: Evil people cannot comprehend what is just, but people who desire to please Yahweh comprehend everything about it.
28.6: It is better to be poor and honest than to be dishonest and rich. \
28.7: Young people who obey Yahweh’s laws are wise, but young people who carouse with gluttons disgrace their fathers.
28.8: Money that people gain by charging an unreasonably large amount of interest from those to whom they loan money will eventually belong to someone who is kind to poor people. \
28.9: Yahweh detests hearing prayers from people who refuse to obey his laws.
28.10: People who guide upright people to act evilly will destroy themselves by what they do, but people whom Yahweh does not blame for acting wickedly will receive what is good. \
28.11: Rich people tend to think that they are wise, but perceptive poor people can tell whether or not this is true.
28.12: People celebrate when righteous people become powerful, but people hide when wicked people become powerful. \
28.13: People who try to hide the sinful things that they do will never be successful, but Yahweh will be merciful to people who confess the sinful things that they have done and stop doing them.
28.14: People who constantly examine how they are thinking and behaving are happy, but bad things will happen to people who become uncaring about those things. \
28.15: Wicked people who rule over poor people are as dangerous as a roaring lion or attacking bear.
28.16: Leaders who are not sensible severely oppress other people, but people who despise gaining wealth unjustly will live for a long time. \
28.17: People who murder others will keep running away from those who would punish them until they die. Do not help them!
28.18: Yahweh will rescue people who continually do what is right, but people who behave dishonestly will ruin themselves in the end. \
28.19: People who work hard will have enough food to eat, but people who waste time doing worthless things will only be poor.
28.20: Yahweh abundantly blesses faithful people, but he will certainly punish people who are eager to be wealthy. \
28.21: Although it is very evil to unfairly favor one person over another, some people will sin by doing so to get even a small bribe.
28.22: People who are eager to become rich are greedy. They do not realize that they will become poor. \
28.23: Afterward, people appreciate someone who has corrected them more than they appreciate someone who has spoken flatteringly to them.
28.24: People who rob their parents and say that doing so is not wrong are as bad as thieves. \
28.25: Greedy people cause people to argue with each other, but Yahweh will prosper people who trust him.
28.26: People who trust in themselves are foolish, but people who act wisely are the ones who will escape what is dangerous. \
28.27: People who give poor people what they need will have all that they need, but there are many who will curse people who ignore poor people.
28.28: People hide when wicked people become powerful, but when those wicked people die, there will be more and more righteous people. \

29.1: Some people remain stubborn even though other people often correct them; but someday something will destroy them quickly, and they will not be able to recover.
29.2: People are joyful when righteous people become influential, but people are miserable when wicked people rule over them. \
29.3: People who cherish what is wise make their fathers happy, but people who have sex with prostitutes waste all their money.
29.4: Kings make the people in their land succeed by acting justly, but leaders who take money dishonestly ruin the people in their land. \
29.5: People who flatter others are really just preparing to exploit them in some way
29.6: Evil people endanger themselves by acting sinfully, but righteous people sing joyfully and are happy. \
29.7: Righteous people know that they should treat poor people justly, but wicked people do not even understand that they should know this.
29.8: People who mock others agitate people throughout a city, but wise people enable others to remain calm. \
29.9: If wise people dispute with foolish people, the foolish people will become angry and sneer and not resolve anything.
29.10: Murderers despise people who always try to do what is right, but righteous people try to protect them. \
29.11: Foolish people uncontrollably express everything that they feel, but wise people control how they express what they feel.
29.12: Leaders who believe the false things that people tell them have only wicked servants. \
29.13: Poor people and the people who oppress them have at least one thing in common: Yahweh is the one who causes both of them to live.
29.14: Kings who judge poor people according to what is true will always rule securely. \
29.15: If parents punish and correct their children, doing so can make those children wise; but if parents let their children do whatever they want to do, then their children will disgrace them.
29.16: People sin more when wicked people rule over them, but someday Yahweh will destroy those wicked people, and righteous people will see it happen. \
29.17: If you discipline your children, then you will no longer feel worried about their behavior and they will make you very happy.
29.18: When the people of a nation do not have messages from Yahweh through his prophets, then they do not control themselves, but people who obey Yahweh’s laws are happy. \
29.19: You cannot correct servants by only speaking to them because they will not do what you say even though they understand what you say.
29.20: Consider this: Foolish people are more likely to do well in life than people who speak thoughtlessly. \
29.21: If you give your servants everything they want when they are young, then they will eventually be arrogant.
29.22: People who easily become angry cause people to argue. Indeed, angry people cause many people to sin. \
29.23: People will humiliate proud people for being proud, but people will honor those who are humble.
29.24: People who take a share of a thief’s spoils greatly endanger themselves; They hear that Yahweh will curse them for not testifying to what they know, but they do not say anything about the crime. \
29.25: Being anxious is as dangerous as walking into a trap, but Yahweh will protect people who trust in him.
29.26: Many people want leaders to help them, but Yahweh is the only one who surely does for them what is just. \
29.27: Righteous people detest unjust people, and wicked people detest people who do the right thing. \

30.1: These are the sayings of Agur son of Jakeh, which Yahweh told him to say; these are what Agur declared to both Ithiel and Ucal:
30.2: I am certainly less intelligent than other people. Indeed, I do not understand as much as everyone else understands!
30.3: I have not learned how to become wise, nor do I know much about Yahweh, the Holy One. \
30.4: But I will say this: Surely nobody has ever gone to heaven and returned to earth! Surely nobody has ever controlled the wind! Surely nobody has ever gathered the water for rain in the clouds! Surely nobody has ever formed the boundaries of the earth! You do not know the name of any such person, or the name of his son. Therefore, you also do not know much! \
30.5: Everything that God says is true; he is like a shield that protects people who trust him to protect them.
30.6: Never claim that God has said something other than what he has actually said. If you do that, then he will correct you and he will prove that you lied about what he said. \
30.7: God, I ask you to do two things; please do them for me before I die:
30.8: Please prevent me from being dishonest or speaking what is not true. Please do not let me become too poor or too rich, but just provide the proper amount of food for me.
30.9: Because if I become rich, I might say that I do not know you and that I do not need you; and if I become poor, I might dishonor you by stealing things. \
30.10: Never say bad things about servants to the people whom they serve. If you do, then they will curse you, and people will hold you responsible for what you said. \
30.12: Some people think that they are sinless, but they have committed disgusting sins, like people who have covered themselves with excrement. \
30.13: Some people are very proud! They think that they are better than other people.
30.14: Some people are very cruel toward others; they harshly oppress and destroy poor people as fierce animals attack and eat other animals. \
30.15: Greedy people are like the offspring of leeches because they always want other people to give them more. There are three, even four things that always want more:
30.16: the place where dead people are, childless women, soil that never receives enough water, and fire that keeps consuming more.
30.17: People who ridicule their fathers, and refuse to obey their mothers deserve to die and have wild animals eat their dead bodies. \
30.18: There are three, even four things, that are too amazing for me to comprehend:
30.19: how a bird flies in the air, how a snake slithers over a rock, how a ship sails in the middle of the ocean, and how a young man loves a young woman. \
30.20: Acting adulterously is as easy for adulterous women as eating and wiping their mouths. Afterward, they claim that they have not sinned at all. \
30.21: There are three, even four, things that the people in the world cannot tolerate:
30.22: what slaves do who become rulers, what worthless people do when they have plenty of food to eat,
30.23: what women whom people hate do when they marry someone, and what servant girls do who replace the wives of their masters. \
30.24: There are four creatures in the world that are small but extremely wise:
30.25: Although ants are not strong, they store up their food during the summer so that they have it to eat during the winter.
30.26: Although hyraxes are also not strong, they are able to make their homes high up in the rocks on cliffs. \
30.27: Although locusts do not have a king, they move in orderly groups like soldiers in an army.
30.28: Although anyone can easily catch lizards in his hands, they can freely enter into kings’ palaces. \
30.29: There are three, even four, things that look very impressive when they walk:
30.30: lions, which are the most powerful animals and never flee from anything,
30.31: strutting male birds, male goats, and kings whom people are afraid to rebel against. \
30.32: If you have acted foolishly by bragging about yourself, or if you were plotting to do what is evil, then stop doing so immediately!
30.33: Stop doing so because just as churning milk produces butter, and squeezing a nose produces blood, making people angry causes them to fight. \

31.1: These are the sayings of King Lemuel; Yahweh had spoken these sayings that his mother had taught him:
31.2: My son, whom I gave birth to and whom I vowed to dedicate to Yahweh, listen to me!
31.3: Do not exhaust yourself by having sex with women; they can destroy kings. \
31.4: Lemuel, kings and dignitaries should not constantly drink wine, or greatly desire to drink what can intoxicate them.
31.5: They must not do this so that they do not forget the laws that they have made and prevent all suffering people from getting what they legally deserve. \
31.6: Let dying people drink what can intoxicate them, and let miserable people drink wine.
31.7: They can drink what can intoxicate them to forget that they are poor and to completely forget what troubles them. \
31.8: Defend those who cannot speak for themselves; defend all those whom others are threatening to kill so that they get what they legally deserve.
31.9: Defend, judge rightly, and plead for suffering and poor people to get what they legally deserve. \
31.10: Virtuous and capable women are difficult to find! This kind of woman is more valuable than precious jewels.
31.11: Her husband completely trusts her, and he will always gain many things because of her.
31.12: Such a woman benefits her husband for as long as she lives. \
31.13: She gets materials to make clothing for both warm and cool weather, and she enjoys making that clothing.
31.14: She is like merchant ships because she brings food to her home from distant places.
31.15: She gets up before dawn in order to prepare food for her family and to prepare some food for her female servants. \
31.16: She carefully evaluates a field and then buys it. Then she uses some of what she earned by working to plant a vineyard in it.
31.17: She keeps her body strong, and she makes her arms strong by working hard. \
31.18: She knows that what she does is very profitable. She works late into the night.
31.19: She makes thread for clothing with her own hands. \
31.20: She generously helps people who are poor and suffering.
31.21: She is not worried that her family will be cold during cold weather because her whole family has the best clothing. \
31.22: She makes her own blankets to cover beds. She wears clothing made from expensive cloth.
31.23: People respect such a woman’s husband at the city gates, when he sits there with the other leaders of the city. \
31.24: This woman makes clothing and sells it. She also sells belts to merchants.
31.25: People notice how strong and dignified she is, and she is cheerful about what will happen in the future. \
31.26: She speaks wisely, and when she speaks, she teaches others to be faithful and kind.
31.27: She carefully watches what happens in her household, and she is never lazy. \
31.28: This woman’s children stand respectfully and declare that she lives well. Her husband says good things about her, as well.
31.29: He says to her, “Many women have acted virtuously and capably, but you indeed have done better than them all!” \
31.30: Charming women who are not good can deceive people into thinking that they are good, and beautiful women will be beautiful for only a short time. However, people will always praise those women who reverently fear Yahweh.
31.31: Give to such women what they have earned, and praise them publicly for what they have done.
